assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational account of how collateral and balance-sheet constraints amplify aggregate fluctuations, with lasting influence on macroeconomic and financial-stability analysis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied the central collateral mechanism, while Gertler's work was crucial to the financial-accelerator framework.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is longstanding, extensively developed theoretically, and central to policy-oriented macro-finance.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of credit among closely related financial-frictions contributions remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law-and-finance research reshaped empirical thinking about investor protection, corporate finance, and financial development across countries.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer, and Vishny formed the core empirical research program; the proposed living laureates capture its principal collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The literature has had several decades of influence and generated a large body of subsequent evidence and institutional research.
uncertainties: Causal interpretation is complicated by legal origins, institutional endogeneity, and heterogeneous later findings.
The original four-person attribution exceeds the maximum number of laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of liquidity, funding constraints, and asset prices has clarified a central channel linking market structure to financial crises and risk premia.
assessment.attribution: Amihud's illiquidity measure and the contributions of Pedersen and Brunnermeier provide distinct, complementary pillars of the nominated theme.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are well established in asset pricing and have gained added relevance through repeated episodes of market stress.
uncertainties: The theme joins several literatures, making its boundaries and the uniquely central contributors contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work made adverse selection empirically measurable and connected insurance-market theory to consequential evidence on market design and policy.
assessment.attribution: Salanie provided major theoretical and empirical foundations, while Finkelstein and Einav made especially influential advances in measurement and applications.
assessment.maturity: The research program is mature, broadly used, and has produced durable methods as well as substantive findings.
uncertainties: The scope of a single unified discovery across insurance settings is broader than any one empirical design.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity transformed modern trade theory and empirical work on selection, productivity, and the gains from trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplied the canonical heterogeneous-firm model, with Helpman and Redding making major connected contributions to its theoretical and empirical development.
assessment.maturity: The framework is highly mature and has become a standard organizing device in international-trade research.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse across a broad heterogeneous-firm literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification established a rigorous alternative to unwarranted point identification and changed credible empirical practice under weak assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the field's central intellectual source, with Tamer and Molinari making important contributions to moment-inequality inference and implementation.
assessment.maturity: The methods are long established and influential across econometrics and applied economics.
uncertainties: The diverse methodological literature makes the boundaries of the proposed joint award debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Information design supplied a powerful general framework for analyzing strategic disclosure, persuasion, and the design of institutions under asymmetric information.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Bergemann are closely associated with Bayesian persuasion, while Morris is central to the related theory of information and strategic interaction.
assessment.maturity: The framework has diffused rapidly through theory and applications, though it is younger than the leading entries.
uncertainties: Its ultimate empirical and policy impact is still developing.
The relation between Bayesian persuasion and the wider information-design literature complicates attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political-economy research on institutions, accountability, and fiscal policy gave systematic analytical content to how political rules shape economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini developed a central joint program, and Besley made foundational complementary contributions on political incentives and state capacity.
assessment.maturity: The body of work is longstanding, influential, and connected to extensive empirical and institutional research.
uncertainties: The candidate label covers several related but distinct research programs.
